context:
Treat Step 3 as a workflow routing change. Required checks are already
minimal, so the implementation should not touch GitHub protection/ruleset
settings. The highest-risk design point is check-name stability: GitHub
required contexts are name-sensitive, and Step 3a may later add an umbrella
result check. Keep the existing required context names stable during Step 3
unless the implementation deliberately leaves rulesets untouched and proves
GitHub still reports the required checks.

Prefer moving whole non-required lanes to a nightly/manual workflow over
sprinkling branch conditions through every job. A split workflow makes
ownership visible: routine develop PR checks prove fast code health, while
nightly/manual checks preserve compatibility and release confidence. If a
job must stay in `test.yml` for status-name compatibility, gate it narrowly
and document the reason next to the condition.
description:
Step 0 invalidated the original strict-base diagnosis. `develop` has no
classic branch protection object, and the active `develop-squash-only`
ruleset already requires only `lint` and `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)`;
`strict_required_status_checks_policy` is already `false`.

The remaining load-bearing Step 3 work is CI-cost reduction, not branch
protection. `.github/workflows/test.yml` still runs a broad non-required
PR-tier workflow on pull requests to `develop`: a multi-version/OS test
matrix, security, smoke/integration lanes, table-format checks, package
install validation, parity, and non-blocking PySpark. The Step 0 baseline
measured recent `Tests` runs at P50 16.70 minutes and P95 19.47 minutes.

Replanned Step 3 should keep the existing required contexts unchanged and
move or gate only non-required heavy lanes so ordinary `develop` PRs stop
spending runner time on release-grade validation. Full validation must
remain available through nightly and workflow_dispatch, and `main` PR/tag
release coverage must remain release-grade.

Designed-together follow-up: Step 3a (`dev-loop-step-3a-path-based-ci-skip`)
remains valid after this replan. Step 3 reduces non-required job breadth for
code PRs; Step 3a separately adds path-aware behavior for content-only PRs
while preserving the already-minimal required contexts.

verifications.command:
repo=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner)
found=0
for ruleset_id in $(gh api "repos/${repo}/rulesets" --jq '.[] | select(.target == "branch" and ((.conditions.ref_name.include // []) | any(. == "refs/heads/develop"))) | .id'); do
  found=1
  gh api "repos/${repo}/rulesets/${ruleset_id}" --jq '.rules[] | select(.type == "required_status_checks") | .parameters'
done
test "$found" = "1"
verifications.description: Develop ruleset still has strict-base off with only the two lightweight required contexts
verifications.expected: strict_required_status_checks_policy is false; required_status_checks are the lightweight develop PR contexts

verifications.description: Classic branch protection is absent or has no conflicting required-check policy
verifications.expected: classic-protection-not-configured OR no broader/strict required checks

verifications.command:
branch=$(git branch --show-current)
pr_base=$(gh pr view "$branch" --json baseRefName --jq .baseRefName)
[ "$pr_base" = "develop" ] || { echo "PR for $branch targets $pr_base, not develop"; exit 1; }
run_id=$(gh run list --workflow test.yml --branch "$branch" --event pull_request --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')
gh run view "$run_id" --json jobs --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion != "skipped") | .name] | sort[]'
verifications.description: Routine develop PR Tests workflow no longer queues broad non-required lanes
verifications.expected: Only non-skipped required/lightweight develop PR job names, plus any explicitly documented lightweight umbrella/content jobs

verifications.command: gh workflow list --json name,state,path --jq '.[] | select((.name | test("nightly|Nightly")) or (.path | test("nightly")))'

work_units.notes:
Choose the smallest maintainable workflow shape that keeps the two
required contexts stable. The default recommendation is:
  - Keep `lint` in its existing workflow.
  - Keep `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)` reporting under the existing Tests
    workflow/job identity for code PRs.
  - Remove, split, or job-gate non-required develop PR lanes from the
    routine `pull_request` path.
  - Preserve label-gated/manual execution for heavier checks when a PR
    intentionally needs them.

Prefer a clear workflow split (`test.yml` for PR-tier required checks,
`nightly.yml` for broad validation) over repeating fragile job-level
conditions everywhere. If a split would break required check names,
use targeted conditions instead and document why.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Kept `.github/workflows/lint.yml` unchanged so the required `lint`
    context stays stable.
  - Replaced the broad `test` matrix with one explicit required job named
    `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)`, preserving the required context while
    avoiding matrix evaluation for routine develop PRs.
  - Added `compat-test` for non-required OS/Python combinations on
    main/push surfaces.
  - Added develop-PR gates to non-required `test.yml` jobs:
    `compat-test`, `check-test-patterns`, `security`,
    `integration-smoke`, `integration-table-formats`, `test-package`,
    `parity`, and `pyspark-tests`.
  - Left `integration` label-gated as-is so `run-integration` can still
    opt a PR into the heavier integration lane intentionally.
work_units.summary: Design the develop PR trigger policy for non-required test.yml jobs

work_units.notes:
Add or update `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` so the jobs removed from
routine develop PRs still run on:
  - `workflow_dispatch`
  - a low-contention nightly schedule

The nightly/manual path should cover the multi-OS/Python matrix,
integration smoke and table-format checks, package install validation,
parity, security audit, and PySpark lane unless w1 finds a specific lane
belongs somewhere else. Use existing commands and dependency setup from
`test.yml`; do not invent a parallel test stack.

If failure issue automation is added, keep it narrow and idempotent:
one open issue per failing nightly class, labeled `incident:nightly-red`,
with the run URL and failing job names. If that automation is too large
for this PR, defer it explicitly and ensure nightly failures are still
visible through GitHub notifications.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Added `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` with `workflow_dispatch` and a
    daily 06:00 UTC schedule.
  - Nightly coverage includes the full OS/Python fast-test matrix,
    patch-safety check, security audit, integration smoke,
    table-format integration, full local integration, package install,
    parity, and non-blocking PySpark lanes.
  - Reused the existing `uv` setup and test commands from `test.yml`.
  - Deferred automatic issue creation to keep this PR scoped; failures
    remain visible through GitHub Actions notifications and manual
    workflow dispatch is available for reruns.
